Blackpool Air Show

One of the biggest free air shows in the country

Flying out over the Irish Sea with the Tower right behind you, the whole of Blackpool on your doorstep, and no ticket needed. Here’s how I would plan a day on the prom, based on what has worked for me.

WhenAugust 2027, dates to be confirmed
EntryFree, no tickets
FlyingAbout 14:00 to 17:40 (2026)
StationBlackpool North, about 15 min walk

Last checked 3 November 2026. Where a time or price says 2026, it’s from last year’s show until the 2027 details are out.

2027 dates to be confirmedBlackpool Air Show is held on a weekend in August. In 2026 it ran on Saturday 8 and Sunday 9 August, and in 2025 on 9 and 10 August. When I last checked, the 2027 dates hadn’t been announced, so I have based the details here on the 2026 show until Visit Blackpool publishes more.

The show at a glance

Blackpool is a free, two day seaside show over the Irish Sea. There are no gates and no tickets, so you can just turn up and find a spot on the promenade. More than 350,000 people were expected over the 2026 weekend, and the prom fills up early, so I would suggest planning your arrival.

The display is flown out over the sea in front of the Tower, roughly between North Pier and Central Pier, and the promenade is closed to traffic for the day. In 2026 the flying ran from about 14:00 to 17:40 on both days, with the RAF Typhoon, the Battle of Britain Memorial Flight, the MiG-17 on its first UK display, US warbirds, the Aerosuperbatics Wingwalkers, Team Raven and plenty of aerobatics. The Red Arrows are usually the headline act, but they missed 2026 because of their North America tour.

Before the flying there’s the Air Show Village on the Tower Festival Headland, with stalls, food, armed forces stands and things for children to do, and around it you have the whole resort: the Tower, the piers, the beach and more chip shops than you can count. I find that makes it a good choice for a mixed group, as not everyone in your party has to love aircraft.

The main things I would think about are getting there early enough to claim a spot near the centre, the road closures on the promenade, and the split tram service on show days. I would advise coming by train if you can. If you drive, parking in one of the big town centre car parks and walking down to the sea has worked well for me.

The Air Show Village

The Air Show Village sits on the Tower Festival Headland, between Central Pier and North Pier, and in 2026 it was open from 11:00 to 18:00 on both days. You’ll find stalls, food, armed forces stands with their ground crews and activities for children, and it sits right behind the best viewing on the promenade.

Children love to see the armed forces stands, and it’s a great way for them to learn about the different roles. If anyone in your group is thinking about joining up, I would suggest asking the crews any questions they have while you are there. Try to walk round it before the flying starts at about 14:00, as it gets very busy once the crowds arrive. This has worked for me in the past.

    Blackpool Air ShowParking & arrival guide

    Blackpool is really built for big crowds. The motorway runs almost to the beach, there are thousands of spaces in the town centre car parks, and Blackpool North station is about 15 minutes’ walk from the Tower. The catch is that the promenade closes to traffic on show days and the trams run in two sections, so it’s best to plan on walking the last few hundred metres. I would advise the train if you can, or arriving by car before 11:00.

    Do I need a ticket?
    No. Blackpool Air Show is free and there are no tickets or gates. You can just find a spot on the promenade. The only things you might pay for are parking, the trams and anything you buy in the Air Show Village.
    Which roads close?
    In 2026 the promenade was closed to all traffic from 10:30 to 19:00 on both days, between Chapel Street and Springfield Road, with signed diversions. That covers the main viewing stretch around Central Pier, the Tower and North Pier, so it is pedestrian only for the day.
    Do the trams run?
    Yes, but not past the display. In 2026 the trams ran in two sections, Starr Gate to Manchester Square every 12 minutes and North Pier to Fleetwood, with extra trams every 7 minutes between Little Bispham and North Station. No trams stopped at the Tower or Central Pier.
    Where can I park?
    In the council car parks. Central car park on Seasiders Way has over 1,300 spaces and is a short walk from Central Pier. South car park and Bloomfield Road are cheaper and a little further out, and Talbot Road multi storey is handy for North Pier. I checked the prices in October 2026, and they may change for event days.
    Is there a park and ride?
    I couldn’t find one for the 2026 show. Blackpool Airport ran a summer park and ride in 2021, but it hasn’t been confirmed since, so take a look at Visit Blackpool closer to the show.
    Can I fly a drone?
    No. A temporary restricted area covers the display, and police seize drones flown inside it. I would leave the drone at home.

    Where to stay

    Blackpool has more hotel beds than almost anywhere in the UK, from big chain hotels by the piers to hundreds of guest houses a few streets back from the sea. Air show weekend is in the middle of the summer holidays, so the sea front fills early. I would advise booking as soon as the dates are confirmed, as this has worked for me in the past.

    Pick Your Day

    With two days of flying and the whole of Blackpool on the doorstep, the air show works really well as a weekend away. You don’t need to watch every display on both days, and I would suggest mixing the flying with the Tower, the piers or the Pleasure Beach. Tell me how long you’re staying and what you enjoy, and I’ll sketch out some days that may suit you.

    Which Day To Pick

    SaturdayIn 2026 the Saturday had the Red Devils parachute team as well as the flying.
    SundayThis is a second full afternoon of flying, and a good back up if the weather is poor on the Saturday.
    The morningThe flying doesn’t start until the afternoon, so mornings are free for the town.
    Early SeptemberThe Illuminations aren’t on during the show. In 2026 they were switched on on 4 September.

    Away From The Show

    Blackpool TowerIt’s the landmark of the whole seafront, with the Tower Ballroom and the view from the top. This is a good one for the morning before the flying.
    The Three PiersNorth, Central and South Pier each have their own feel, from a gentle stroll to rides and arcades.
    Pleasure BeachThe big rides and rollercoasters at the south end of the prom. I would advise booking ahead on a busy weekend.
    Stanley ParkA big green park inland, with a boating lake and gardens. This may work for you if you fancy a quieter afternoon away from the crowds.

    Help On Show Days

    The air show fills miles of promenade over two days, so it’s easy to lose each other in the crowd or get caught out by the weather. Here’s what I would do if something goes wrong, plus quick answers to the questions I see asked most. I hope it helps you plan.

    More helpIf the forecast looks grim, have a look at my rainy day plan. If you or someone in your group finds noise and crowds hard, my calm visit guide may help. And for the end of the day, there’s getting home from an airshow.
    In an emergency, call 999. For anything else, ask the nearest steward or police officer. They can point you to first aid and help you find someone.

    If Something Goes Wrong

    Lost Each Other

    Phone signal can be poor on a packed prom, so I would advise agreeing a meeting point before you split up. The Tower is easy to find from anywhere on the front. A band or label with your number on is a good idea for younger children, and please tell a steward or police officer straight away if someone goes missing.

    Feeling Unwell

    Any steward or police officer can direct you to first aid. There’s almost no shade on the prom, so I would suggest taking breaks in the cafes behind the front on a hot afternoon.

    Flying Times

    The display times for each day go online before the show, and the show radio on DAB carries the commentary. Details are in .

    Bad Weather

    Sea mist, low cloud or a strong wind off the Irish Sea can change the flying at short notice. It’s a two day show, so if one day looks poor, I would think about going on the other.

    Getting Home

    The promenade stays closed to traffic until early evening and the trams run as a split service, so the stations get very busy straight after the flying. I would suggest staying for tea in town while the crowds clear. See .

    Loud Aircraft

    The Typhoon is very loud, and the noise bounces off the sea wall and the buildings along the front. I would advise ear defenders for babies, toddlers and anyone sensitive to noise.

    Quick Answers

    Is it really free?

    Yes. There are no tickets, so you can just turn up on the promenade.

    When are the 2027 dates?

    They haven’t been announced yet. The show is usually in August, and in 2026 it ran on Saturday 8 and Sunday 9 August.

    What time does the flying start?

    In 2026 the flying ran from about 14:00 to 17:40, with the Air Show Village open from 11:00 to 18:00. The 2027 times will come out nearer the show.

    Can I bring my dog?

    From 1 May to 30 September dogs aren’t allowed on the beach between North Pier and the Mirror Ball opposite the Solaris Centre, and they must be on a lead on the promenade between North and South Piers. Guide dogs are exempt. The crowds and the jets are loud, so I would think carefully before bringing your dog.

    Can I drink alcohol on the prom?

    No. There’s a ban on drinking in public on the promenade, and glass isn’t allowed on the beach or the sea wall.

    Can I fly my drone?

    No. Drones aren’t allowed in the restricted area over the display.

    Where are the toilets?

    There are promenade toilets, including the Undercroft at North Pier, and Changing Places toilets at the Holiday Inn on Talbot Road and the Solaris Centre and Harrowside on the promenade. Full details in .

    Are the trams running?

    Yes, but the promenade closes to traffic and the trams run as a split service while the show is on. See for the details.

    Where can I park?

    The council car parks fill early, and the prom roads close from mid morning, so I would advise coming by train if you can. Blue Badge holders get 3 hours free in most council car parks. More in .

    Can I watch from the beach?

    Yes, but not right in front of the Tower. A bit before the air display starts, the beach between North Pier and Central Pier is cleared and closed. South of Central Pier the beach stays open, so if you want to be on the sand for the flying, I would head that way and keep an eye on the tide.

    Can I watch from North Pier?

    You can, but it isn’t free on show days. When I last went, North Pier charged a fiver to go on, searched your bags, and you weren’t allowed to take your own food and drink, so you have to buy theirs. I would leave the picnic for the prom.

    Can I camp on the beach?

    No. Camping and tents overnight aren’t allowed, so please see the rules before you go. Have a look at for places nearby.

    Are the Illuminations on?

    Not during the air show. In 2026 the Illuminations were switched on on 4 September, a few weeks after the show.

    I don’t have an answer for that here. The official Visit Blackpool air show page may help.

    The 2027 details may change, so please check before you go. I will update this guide when I can.

    Pick your spot

    The whole promenade faces west over the Irish Sea, and the display is centred roughly in front of the Tower, between North Pier and Central Pier. What changes is how close you are to the centre, how much space you get, and how near you are to the Air Show Village, food and toilets. Think about what matters most to your group.

    Filter by feature

    Shooting at Blackpool

    The crowd faces west over the Irish Sea. The sun is behind you in the morning, beside you on your left in the early afternoon, and in front of you from about mid afternoon, which is when much of the flying happens. Displays are flown further out than at an airfield, so I would suggest 400 to 600mm.

    Get creative on the sea front

    At Blackpool you get the Tower and the piers with the sea behind them, which you just won’t find at an airfield. The catch is the light, as the sun moves in front of you through the afternoon. I would suggest using the sun guide to plan where you stand, and treating the later displays as a chance for silhouettes, smoke and sparkle on the water.

    Ideas to try

    • Try walking out on Central Pier, or North Pier if you don’t mind paying the fiver it charges on show days, and look back along the display line, so you can get aircraft with the Tower or the other pier in the frame.
    • Later in the afternoon, you can turn the backlight into a feature. I would expose for the sky and go for silhouettes, smoke trails and sun on the water.
    • I would stand south of the Tower, towards Central Pier, so more of the display is to your right and away from the sun.
    • I like to leave room in the frame for smoke, so it leads the eye to the aircraft.
    • You can try zooming out now and then to include the crowd, the beach or the Tower, so the photo says Blackpool.

    Starting settings

    Pick what’s flying and the weather for a starting point. It uses 1/1250 as a benchmark for the fastest shutter, at least double your focal length, and keeps ISO at 1200 or below, so the files stay clean and the shutter stays realistic for the subject. After the first pass, I like to check the histogram and adjust from there.

The flying doesn’t usually start until the afternoon, so I would suggest giving them a mission for the morning. Here’s a spotting card they can tick off as they go, and children love to see how many they can find.

    Making The Day Easier

    It’s free

    There are no tickets to buy for anyone, so you can come and go as the kids need.

    The buses

    In 2026, children travelled free on Blackpool Transport buses in August. I would advise checking if the offer is back for 2027.

    Ear defenders

    Your child’s ears are delicate, so try to protect them as much as possible. I would recommend ear defenders for babies and toddlers, especially for the Typhoon.

    A morning on the sand

    If the tide is out, the beach is a brilliant place to burn off energy in the morning. The stretch between North Pier and Central Pier is cleared a bit before the flying starts, so I would move up to the prom then, or head south of Central Pier where the beach stays open.

    Sun and shade

    There’s almost no shade on the prom, so sun cream, hats and plenty of water are a must for me.

    Things to do

    See what’s on for families in .

    Jack’s tipI would suggest keeping the kids close to your pitch once the flying starts. The prom gets very busy in the afternoon, and it’s much easier to stay together than to find each other again.

    Food, toilets & access

    This is a seaside resort, so food, drink and toilets are never far away. The Air Show Village has its own food stalls, and there are cafes, chip shops and pubs all along the front and in the streets behind it. You’ll find the queues peak just before the flying starts.

    Good To Know

    The quick answers I get asked most about Blackpool Air Show. I last checked these on 3 November 2026, so I would still look at the show’s own rules before you go.

    YesCheck firstNo
    1. Pushchairs And BuggiesYesFlat promenade

      It’s a public seafront and the prom is flat and paved, so a pushchair is fine. It gets packed near the Tower in the afternoon, so I would find your spot early.

    2. DogsCheck firstOn a lead

      From May to September dogs aren’t allowed on the beach between North Pier and the Mirror Ball, and they must be on a lead on the prom between North and South Piers. The jets are loud, so I would think carefully before bringing yours.

    3. Your Own Food And DrinkYesPicnics, no alcohol

      Bring a picnic for the prom if you like. North Pier is different on show days, as you can’t take your own food and drink on, so you have to buy theirs. Drinking alcohol in public is banned on the promenade, and glass isn’t allowed on the beach or the sea wall.

    4. Gazebos, Windbreaks And ChairsCheck firstNot confirmed yet

      Folding chairs and blankets are fine. I couldn’t find a rule on gazebos or windbreaks for the show, so I would ask before you take anything big, as space by the sea wall gets tight.

    5. Water Refill PointsCheck firstNot confirmed yet

      I couldn’t find any refill points for the show. There’s almost no shade on the prom, so I would bring more water than you think you’ll need, in plastic bottles.

    6. Changing Places ToiletYesHoliday Inn, Talbot Road

      There’s a council Changing Places toilet at the Holiday Inn on Talbot Gateway, open 08:00 to 20:00 in summer and about 10 minutes’ walk from the front. The prom toilets have accessible loos on a RADAR key.

    1. Carers' TicketsYesNo tickets needed

      The show is free for everyone, so there’s no carer ticket to sort out. You just turn up.

    2. Hearing SupportCheck firstNot confirmed yet

      I couldn’t find anything on hearing loops or BSL for the show. I would ask Visit Blackpool before you go if you need support.

    3. Quiet AreaCheck firstNot confirmed yet

      I couldn’t find a calm or sensory space for the show. If someone needs a break from the noise, the streets back from the front are much quieter than the prom.

    4. Re-entryYesFree to come and go

      It’s an open public seafront with no gates, so you can wander off into town and come back whenever you like.

    5. First Aid And Lost ChildrenCheck firstEvent first aiders

      There are event first aiders, and any steward or police officer can point you to them. I couldn’t find a lost children point for 2026, so I would agree a meeting point like the Tower and put your number on younger ones.

    6. If It RainsCheck firstGoes ahead, weather allowing

      Unfortunately the weather on the day will be what it will be, so plan accordingly. If it’s fresh, dress in layers to keep warm. It’s a two day show, so if one day looks poor the other may be better.

    Food & drink

    There are food stalls in the Air Show Village, plus hundreds of cafes, chippies and restaurants in the town. Picnics are fine, but the promenade has a ban on drinking alcohol in public, and glass isn’t allowed on the beach or sea wall.

    Toilets

    Promenade toilets, including the Undercroft at North Pier, open 08:00 to 20:00 in summer, with accessible toilets on a RADAR key. I would go before the flying starts, and if you aren’t waiting for a particular display, use that slot as your break.

    Shade and seating

    There is almost no shade on the prom, so I would bring hats, sun cream and your own chairs. The sea wall steps make a handy seat if you get there early.

    Kids’ activities

    There are activities in the Air Show Village, and the beach south of Central Pier stays open during the flying. The Tower, the piers and the arcades are nearby if they need a break.

    Accessibility
    The promenade is flat and paved, and the trams are wheelchair accessible. Blue Badge holders get 3 hours free with a clock in most council car parks, and Central car park has 42 Blue Badge spaces. Accessible toilets along the prom use a RADAR key, and there are Changing Places toilets at the Holiday Inn on Talbot Gateway, about 10 minutes’ walk from the front, and the Solaris Centre and Harrowside on the promenade (FY1 1NE). When I last checked both were open 08:00 to 20:00 in summer. I couldn’t find a dedicated accessible viewing area, so I would advise arriving early for a clear spot by the sea wall.
    What can I bring?
    Folding chairs, blankets, food and soft drinks. There’s no drinking alcohol in public on the promenade, as police and council staff can confiscate it, no glass on the beach or sea wall, no camping or tents overnight, and no drones in the restricted area over the display. Please see the rules before you go.
    Display times and commentary
    The display times for each day go online before the show, and a show radio station on DAB carries the commentary and traffic updates.
    Medical help
    Ask any steward or police officer and they will point you to the nearest first aid point.
    The tide
    If you sit on the sand, it’s worth keeping an eye on the tide. On a big high tide the sea comes up to the sea wall, so be ready to move up to the promenade. The weather box on the Plan your day tab shows the approximate tide times.
    If the weather turns
    Low cloud, sea mist or strong wind can change the programme or stop some displays. It is a two day show, so if Saturday looks poor, Sunday may be better. I would pack a waterproof either way.
